t: Which of the following is a fictitious asset?
o: Discount on issue of debentures not yet written off
Investment in government securities
Goodwill purchased in an acquisition
Prepaid rent
e: Fictitious assets are deferred expenses or losses shown on the asset side only because they have not yet been written off; purchased goodwill is a genuine intangible asset.

t: Cash withdrawn by the proprietor from the business for personal use is recorded as:
o: Revenue of the business
Drawings, which reduce the owner's capital
An expense in the profit and loss account
A loan to the proprietor shown as a fixed asset
e: Under the entity concept, drawings are a withdrawal of the owner's investment and not a business expense, so they are deducted from capital.

t: Which group of users of financial statements is primarily interested in an insurer's solvency and ability to pay claims?
o: Advertising agencies
Policyholders and the regulator (IRDAI)
Trade creditors seeking payment for stationery
Employees seeking bonus
e: Policyholders depend on the insurer's long-term ability to honour claims and IRDAI monitors solvency to protect them; other users have narrower interests.

t: A general insurer purchases office furniture on credit for ₹4 lakh. The effect on the accounting equation is:
o: Only assets change: furniture up and cash down by ₹4 lakh
Assets increase by ₹4 lakh and liabilities increase by ₹4 lakh
Assets increase by ₹4 lakh and capital increases by ₹4 lakh
Assets and liabilities both decrease by ₹4 lakh
e: A credit purchase of an asset increases both the asset (furniture) and the liability (creditor); cash is unaffected until payment.

topic: Accounting Process and Books of Accounts
t: The brief explanation written below a journal entry describing the transaction is called:
o: Narration
Ledger folio
Casting
Posting reference
e: Narration explains the nature of the entry; ledger folio is the page reference of the ledger account to which the entry is posted.

topic: Accounting Process and Books of Accounts
t: A machine costing ₹6,00,000 was purchased on 1 October 2025. Depreciation is charged at 10% per annum on the straight-line method pro rata to the period of use. Depreciation for the year ended 31 March 2026 is:
e: The machine was in use for six months, so depreciation = 6,00,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹30,000.

topic: Accounting Process and Books of Accounts
t: A standing instruction payment of ₹18,000 for an electricity bill was debited by the bank but not yet recorded in the cash book. In a bank reconciliation statement starting from the favourable balance as per cash book, this amount is:
o: Ignored, since it is a bank error
Added, since the cash book is understated
Added as a contra entry
Deducted, since the bank balance is lower than the cash book balance
e: The bank has already reduced the balance; the cash book has not, so the amount is deducted from the cash book balance to reach the pass book balance.

topic: Accounting Process and Books of Accounts
t: At year end, debtors stand at ₹8,00,000 and a provision for doubtful debts of 5% is to be created. The existing provision is ₹25,000. The amount to be charged to the profit and loss account for the year is:
e: Required provision = 5% × 8,00,000 = ₹40,000; since ₹25,000 already exists, only the additional ₹15,000 is charged to the P&L account.

topic: Accounting Process and Books of Accounts
t: Outstanding salary of ₹1,20,000 at the year end is adjusted in the final accounts by:
o: Deducting it from salary in the profit and loss account
Adding it to salary in the profit and loss account and showing it as a current liability in the balance sheet
Showing it as a current asset in the balance sheet
Showing it only as a liability without affecting the profit and loss account
e: Under the accrual basis the expense belongs to the current year even though unpaid, so it is both expensed and recognised as a liability.

t: Under AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment), the cost of an item of PPE includes:
o: Interest on working capital borrowings of the company
Purchase price including duties and taxes (net of recoverable taxes) and directly attributable costs of bringing the asset to working condition
All administrative overheads of the year of purchase
Expected future repair costs over the life of the asset
e: Only costs directly attributable to acquisition and installation are capitalised; general overheads and future repairs are revenue in nature.

t: As per Section 96 of the Companies Act 2013, every company (other than a one-person company) must hold its annual general meeting within:
o: Six months from the close of the financial year
Three months from the close of the financial year
Twelve months from the close of the financial year
Nine months from the close of the financial year
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The AGM must be held within six months of the financial year end and the gap between two AGMs may not exceed fifteen months; nine months applies only to the first AGM.

t: Under AS 16, borrowing costs directly attributable to the construction of a qualifying asset are:
o: Capitalised as part of the cost of the asset until it is ready for its intended use
Credited to capital reserve
Always charged to the profit and loss account as incurred
Deferred and written off over five years
e: AS 16 requires capitalisation of borrowing costs on qualifying assets during the construction period; other borrowing costs are expensed.

t: A company with net profit after tax and preference dividend of ₹45 crore and 15 crore equity shares outstanding throughout the year reports a basic EPS under AS 20 of:
e: Basic EPS = profit attributable to equity shareholders ÷ weighted average equity shares = 45/15 = ₹3 per share.

t: Under AS 19, a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards incidental to ownership of an asset is classified as:
o: A hire-purchase contract
An operating lease
A sale and leaseback
A finance lease
e: Finance leases are capitalised by the lessee as an asset with a corresponding liability; operating leases are expensed on a straight-line basis.

t: Under Section 92 of the Companies Act 2013, every company must file with the Registrar an annual return containing:
o: Its income tax computation
Particulars of its registered office, shareholding, directors, meetings and indebtedness as at the close of the financial year
The list of its insurance policies
The minutes of all Board meetings
e: The annual return (Form MGT-7) is a snapshot of the company's structure and governance; financial statements are filed separately under Section 137.

t: Under Section 152 of the Companies Act 2013, in a public company at every AGM:
o: All directors must retire and seek re-election
Independent directors must retire by rotation
At least one-third of the directors liable to retire by rotation shall retire
No director can retire unless removed by shareholders
e: Not less than two-thirds of total directors must be liable to retire by rotation, and one-third of those retire at each AGM; independent directors are excluded from rotation.

t: A debenture issued by a company represents:
o: A right to receive dividend in priority to preference shares
A deposit accepted from the public without interest
A share in the ownership of the company
An acknowledgment of debt carrying a fixed rate of interest, usually secured on the company's assets
e: Debenture holders are creditors, not members; interest is payable irrespective of profits and is a charge, whereas dividend is an appropriation.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company, following the 2021 amendment to the Insurance Act, is:
e: The Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 raised the FDI cap from 49% to 74% subject to safeguards; the Schedule 5A disclosure shows the resulting shareholding pattern.

t: Under IRDAI's corporate governance norms, the Risk Management Committee of an insurer is expected to:
o: Approve the insurer's advertising campaigns
Settle disputed claims above a threshold
Appoint the Appointed Actuary
Oversee the risk management strategy, including the appointment of a Chief Risk Officer and review of the asset-liability position
e: The RMC assists the Board in establishing the risk framework and monitoring material risks; claims, marketing and actuarial appointments are handled by other functions.

t: Section 27A of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits an insurer from:
o: Investing in listed equity shares
Investing in Central Government securities
Investing policyholders' funds outside India
Holding deposits with scheduled banks
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 27A read with Section 27 restricts investment of controlled funds to assets in India; the other three are permitted approved categories.

t: Section 10 of the Insurance Act 1938 requires an insurer carrying on more than one class of business to:
o: Register a separate company for each class
Maintain a single consolidated fund for all classes
Obtain a separate licence from the Reserve Bank for each class
Keep separate accounts of all receipts and payments in respect of each class of insurance business
e: Separation of accounts by class (and the separate revenue accounts for fire, marine and miscellaneous) flows from Section 10; life insurers must additionally keep a separate life fund.

t: A general insurer issues a two-year engineering policy on 1 April 2025 for a total premium of ₹24 lakh covering the whole period. In the revenue account for the year ended 31 March 2026, premium earned from this policy is:
o: ₹24 lakh
₹6 lakh
Nil until the policy expires
₹12 lakh
e: Premium is recognised over the period of risk; half the period has run, so ₹12 lakh is earned and ₹12 lakh is carried as reserve for unexpired risk.

t: Cash and bank balances of a general insurer, including deposit accounts and cheques in hand, are disclosed in:
o: Schedule 9
Schedule 12
Schedule 8
Schedule 11
e: Schedule 11 covers cash, bank balances and money at call; Schedule 8 is investments, Schedule 9 loans and Schedule 12 advances and other assets.

t: In the Profit and Loss Account of a general insurer, which of the following is an appropriation rather than a charge?
o: Interest on subordinated debt
Transfer to general reserve
Expenses other than those related to insurance business
Provision for diminution in value of investments
e: Appropriations (dividend, transfers to reserves) are made after arriving at profit after tax; provisions, non-insurance expenses and interest are charges in arriving at profit.

t: Under IRDAI norms, premium ceded to reinsurers under a treaty is recognised in the cedant's revenue account:
o: At the end of the treaty year
As an operating expense in Schedule 4
Only when the reinsurer confirms the quarterly statement
In the same period in which the related direct premium is recognised, as a deduction from gross premium
e: Reinsurance premium ceded is matched with the direct premium to which it relates, so net written premium reflects the insurer's true retention for the period.

t: Which of the following disclosures is mandated by IRDAI in a general insurer's financial statements?
o: The internal audit plan for the next year
A list of branch addresses
Age-wise analysis of claims outstanding and the number of claims settled, intimated and outstanding during the year
Details of all agency agreements
e: IRDAI requires disclosures on claims ageing, claims settled and outstanding, encumbrances, commitments, contingent liabilities and related party transactions in the notes.

t: A general insurer's fire revenue account shows gross direct premium ₹400 crore, reinsurance accepted ₹20 crore, reinsurance ceded ₹140 crore, opening URR ₹130 crore and closing URR ₹150 crore. Claims incurred (net) ₹160 crore, net commission (₹10 crore, i.e. net commission income), operating expenses ₹70 crore. The underwriting result (excluding investment income) is:
o: Profit of ₹40 crore
Profit of ₹60 crore
Profit of ₹20 crore
Loss of ₹40 crore
e: Net written premium = 400 + 20 − 140 = 280; premium earned = 280 − (150 − 130) = ₹260 crore; result = 260 − 160 + 10 − 70 = ₹40 crore profit (net commission income is added).

t: Under a 'stop loss' treaty covering losses in excess of a 90% loss ratio up to 120%, an insurer's net premium for the year is ₹500 crore and net claims are ₹550 crore. The recovery from the reinsurer is:
o: ₹150 crore
₹100 crore
₹550 crore
₹50 crore
e: Actual loss ratio = 550/500 = 110%; the treaty responds for the layer above 90% and up to 120%, so recovery = (110% − 90%) × 500 = ₹100 crore.

t: A general insurer earned investment income of ₹900 crore on average investment assets of ₹12,000 crore. Its investment yield is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Investment yield = investment income ÷ average investments = 900/12,000 = 7.5%.

t: Under a quota share treaty of 30% with a ceding commission of 25%, an insurer cedes premium on a portfolio of ₹200 crore. The net cash flow to the reinsurer in respect of premium (before claims) is:
o: ₹45 crore
₹15 crore
₹60 crore
₹50 crore
e: Premium ceded = 30% × 200 = ₹60 crore; ceding commission = 25% × 60 = ₹15 crore; net amount payable to the reinsurer = ₹45 crore.

t: Every Indian insurer must file its reinsurance programme for the ensuing financial year with IRDAI:
o: Once every five years
Before the commencement of the financial year, along with a Board-approved reinsurance policy
Only after a major loss occurs
Within six months after the end of the financial year
e: IRDAI's reinsurance regulations require the Board-approved programme to be filed in advance (at least 45 days before the year begins) and subsequent changes to be reported.

t: An 'unexpired risk reserve' and a 'premium deficiency reserve' differ in that:
o: URR defers unearned premium to the unexpired period, whereas premium deficiency provides for expected losses beyond that deferred premium
URR is computed only for marine business
URR is a shareholders' reserve while premium deficiency is a technical reserve
Premium deficiency is created from profits as an appropriation
e: URR is a mechanical deferral of premium; premium deficiency is an additional liability recognised when URR is insufficient to meet expected claims and expenses for the unexpired period.

t: A 'cut-through clause' in a reinsurance contract provides that:
o: The reinsurer's liability is cut to half after one year
The cedant may stop ceding risks once the premium limit is reached
The reinsurer will pay its share of a claim directly to the policyholder if the ceding insurer becomes insolvent
The reinsurer may cancel the treaty mid-term without notice
e: Normally the policyholder has no contractual relationship with the reinsurer; a cut-through clause creates such a direct right in the event of the cedant's insolvency.

t: For solvency purposes, subordinated debt raised by an insurer as 'other forms of capital':
o: Is fully treated as equity capital in computing ASM
Is included in available solvency margin only to the extent and in the manner permitted by IRDAI, and not as ordinary equity
Is entirely ignored in computing solvency
Is treated as a technical reserve
e: IRDAI allows limited recognition of subordinated debt and preference capital in ASM (within prescribed caps relative to net worth), reflecting its lower loss-absorbing quality than equity.

t: A general insurer's gross premium in a segment is ₹2,000 crore and net premium is ₹1,400 crore; the prescribed factor for gross premium in that segment is 0.70. Using the 20% rule, RSM-1 for the segment is:
o: ₹196 crore
₹400 crore
₹280 crore
₹600 crore
e: Higher of (gross premium × factor) = 2,000 × 0.70 = 1,400 and net premium 1,400 is ₹1,400 crore; RSM-1 = 20% × 1,400 = ₹280 crore.

t: The 'solvency ratio' of an insurer is defined as:
o: Total assets divided by total liabilities
Shareholders' funds divided by gross premium
Net premium divided by net worth
Available solvency margin divided by required solvency margin
e: The ratio compares the excess of assets over liabilities with the regulatory minimum margin; IRDAI requires it to be at least 1.5.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
o: 1 hour
3 hours
6 hours
24 hours
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: Which of the following statements about the solvency framework for Indian general insurers is INCORRECT?
o: The required solvency margin is computed as a flat 20% of the insurer's net worth
IRDAI is moving towards a risk-based capital framework
IRDAI may prescribe a higher solvency requirement for a specific insurer based on its risk profile
The solvency margin must be maintained at all times, not merely at the year end
e: RSM is derived from premiums and claims with segment-wise factors, not from net worth; the other statements correctly describe the current framework and its direction.

t: The Investment Committee of a general insurer must include:
o: At least two non-executive directors, the CEO, the CFO, the Chief Investment Officer, the Chief Risk Officer and the Appointed Actuary
Only independent directors
The statutory auditor as chairperson
Representatives of the insurer's custodian
e: IRDAI prescribes this composition to combine Board oversight with executive accountability; auditors and custodians are outside parties and cannot be members.

t: Investments in 'infrastructure' for the purpose of IRDAI's investment pattern are those in:
o: Sectors covered by the harmonised master list of infrastructure sub-sectors notified by the Government of India
Only Central Government projects
Any listed company with a market capitalisation above ₹10,000 crore
Shares of the insurer's promoter companies
e: IRDAI aligns the definition of infrastructure with the Government's harmonised master list (roads, power, ports, telecom, etc.), which also carries higher group exposure limits.

t: Which of the following would be classified as 'other investments' rather than 'approved investments' for a general insurer?
o: Bonds of a State Government
Treasury bills of the Government of India
Equity shares of a listed company that has not paid the required dividend in the preceding years
AAA-rated bonds of a public sector bank
e: Equity not meeting the dividend track-record criterion, debt rated below AA and unlisted instruments fall under other investments, which are capped at 15% of investment assets.

t: Under IRDAI norms, the investment function of an insurer is subject to:
o: Daily reporting of every transaction to IRDAI
Annual reporting only, with the audited accounts
Quarterly reporting to IRDAI through prescribed investment returns and periodic internal/concurrent audit
No reporting unless losses are incurred
e: Insurers file quarterly investment returns (category-wise holdings, exposure, downgrades, NPAs) and have the function audited as prescribed.

t: A general insurer holds 8% Government of India bonds purchased at ₹105 per ₹100 face value with 5 years to maturity. Under IRDAI valuation norms, the premium of ₹5 is:
o: Credited to the fair value change account
Ignored, with the bond carried at ₹105 until maturity
Written off entirely in the year of purchase
Amortised over the remaining 5 years, reducing the carrying value each year
e: Debt securities are carried at amortised cost; the premium is written down to par over the remaining maturity, so interest income is effectively reduced to the yield to maturity.

t: An insurer's investment policy approved by the Board must, among other things, address:
o: Asset-liability management, liquidity, prudential norms, exposure limits and risk management of the investment portfolio
Premium rates for motor third party insurance
Agents' commission structure
The branch network expansion plan
e: The investment policy sets the framework within which the Investment Committee operates; pricing, commission and distribution are outside its scope.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
o: 24 months
36 months
48 months
60 months
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: Following the GST Council's decision effective 22 September 2025, premium on individual health insurance policies is:
o: Taxed at 12%
Exempt from GST
Taxed at 18%
Taxed at 5% with input tax credit
e: Individual life and health insurance premiums were exempted from GST from 22 September 2025; group and most general insurance lines continue to attract 18%.

t: The internal audit function of an insurer is primarily intended to:
o: Replace the statutory audit required under the Insurance Act
Certify the financial statements for shareholders
Provide independent assurance to the Board and audit committee on the adequacy of internal controls and risk management
Prepare the tax return of the company
e: Internal audit is a management tool reporting to the audit committee; the statutory audit under Section 12 of the Insurance Act remains a separate external requirement.

t: Financial statement analysis using ratios is limited because:
o: Ratios are based on historical cost figures and can be distorted by differences in accounting policies
Ratios are not permitted under the Companies Act
Ratios always predict future performance accurately
Ratios can only be computed for listed companies
e: Ratios are useful for comparison and trend analysis but must be interpreted with knowledge of accounting policies, inflation and industry context.

t: An insurer settled 9,200 claims during the year out of 10,000 claims available for settlement (opening outstanding plus intimated). Its claims settlement ratio is:
e: Claims settlement ratio = claims settled ÷ claims available for settlement = 9,200/10,000 = 92%; a higher ratio indicates faster claims service.

t: A general insurer has net written premium of ₹6,000 crore and net worth of ₹2,000 crore. Its underwriting leverage (net premium to net worth) is:
o: 0.33 times
6.0 times
3.0 times, indicating that each rupee of capital supports three rupees of retained premium
e: Underwriting leverage = net written premium ÷ net worth = 6,000/2,000 = 3; higher leverage means greater strain on capital from underwriting volatility.
